proposals.rationale: The spec/contract requirement is correct and agreed: initialize() MUST return an error (NotInitialized) when the mandatory IEvictionPolicy receptacle is unbound. The code violates it: initialize() calls get_pool_id() first (src/lib.rs:68), and get_pool_id does self.eviction_policy.get().unwrap() (src/lib.rs:55), which panics on an unbound receptacle before the graceful map_err(NotInitialized) guard at :69-71 is ever reached. The same unwrap-on-unbound pattern recurs in create_memory_tier_entry (:392), recover_extent (:573), and via get_pool_id in oldest_keys (:373). Correct spec + buggy code => ALIGN task, no code edit and no spec change.

proposals.related: US1 Acceptance Scenario 3; Edge Cases bullet 1
proposals.rationale: The spec is correct and agreed: create_memory_tier_entry with a null pointer MUST return an error and record no entry (US1/AS3 + Edge Cases). The code validates only size == 0 (InvalidSize, src/lib.rs:387-389); there is no null-pointer guard, so a null *mut u8 is accepted and an entry is recorded. No null-pointer error variant exists on DispatchMapError. Correct spec + buggy code => ALIGN task, no code edit and no spec change.

reuse_count is a real, working, intentional per-entry field on DispatchEntry (AtomicU32) that is incremented on every read-reference acquisition (lookup, take_read, downgrade_reference) and read only in the Debug impl. It is unspecced. Per Phase B policy for dispatch-map (1 unspecced => BACKFILL), the spec is brought up to reality by adding FR-029 describing the counter as built (internal instrumentation, no IDispatchMap accessor), updating the Dispatch Entry key entity, and adding acceptance scenarios to User Stories 2 and 4. The field is already part of the documented 56-byte DispatchEntry layout (FR-028), so SC-004 is unaffected.
proposals.before: spec.md had no requirement covering reuse_count. Key Entities > Dispatch Entry: "Holds the location (Location enum), size in 4KiB blocks, read reference count (u32), write reference count (u32), and an EvictionHandle ... Protected by Mutex/Condvar. Under the integrity-check feature it additionally carries a 4-byte CRC-32 checksum field ..." (no reuse_count).
proposals.after: Added FR-029: "Each DispatchEntry MUST carry a per-entry reuse_count (AtomicU32), initialized to 0 when the entry is created (via create_memory_tier_entry, recover_extent, or the recovery walk in initialize) and incremented by 1 (relaxed atomic ordering) on each operation that acquires a read reference on the entry: lookup, take_read, and downgrade_reference. Operations that do not acquire a read reference (take_write, release_read, release_write, convert_to_storage, and the tier-transition methods) MUST NOT modify it. The counter is internal read-hit instrumentation: it is surfaced only through the DispatchEntry Debug representation and MUST NOT be exposed through any IDispatchMap method. It does not participate in eviction ordering (delegated to IEvictionPolicy) or in reference-count semantics." Updated Dispatch Entry key entity to list the reuse_count (AtomicU32) field. Added US2/AS6 and US4/AS9 acceptance scenarios covering the increment behavior.
